scope: CrossFlow v1 money path: funding, internal batch settlement, composed residual routing, recovery

reviews.reviewer: independent review agent, no prior context, static review

findings.summary: The local buy-and-sell-same-stock case was rejected by the ordering rule before reaching the no-round-trip guard, so that guard was labelled tested but unexercised.
findings.fix: Ascending cross tuples plus widened cash bounds so the round-trip rule is what fires.

findings.summary: Rust accepted a one-owner batch that the off-chain validator and the spec reject, a permissionless no-op state transition.
findings.fix: settle_batch requires batch_count >= 2; single-owner settlement stays on the owner-signed thin path.

findings.summary: Bytes appended after the declared body were ignored by the argument decoder.
findings.fix: Exact top-level instruction length is authenticated through the instructions sysvar.

findings.summary: Rust capped intermediate debits at MAX_POOL_AMOUNT while the TS model caps at MAX_AMOUNT.
findings.fix: No acceptance difference: debit <= funding <= MAX_AMOUNT is enforced in both.

findings.summary: The settled event emitted three rows regardless of batch_count.
findings.fix: Event matrices are truncated to the participating rows.

findings.summary: The checker recomputed the binary hash but never compared it, and the legacy-size claim was prose only.
findings.fix: The checker binds the built binary and the committed manifest, and the demo records the measured legacy size.

findings.summary: Several spec-required negatives had no local transcript case.
findings.fix: Six more negatives added; the matrix is now fourteen named rejections.

reviews.reviewer: independent review agent, no prior context, static review

findings.summary: The on-chain residual decoder read a fixed three weights regardless of batch_count, so a two-owner routed body from the shipping client could not decode and a crafted one fed a phantom weight into the allocation.
findings.fix: The decoder reads exactly batch_count weights; unit tests cover a two-owner residual and a truncated one.

findings.summary: load_group was not in fact shared with settle_batch, and it substituted values in the mint-authority slots, making the routed path validate mints more weakly than the internal path.
findings.fix: settle_batch calls load_group; the loader reads the real COption tags and fails closed on a short mint account.

findings.summary: The evidence checker compared two generator-written fields, never asserted the payout array length, and read the committed policy from decoded JSON.
findings.fix: The checker recomputes the venue quote, rebuilds every payout from funding plus cross plus residual, re-hashes the recorded policy bytes and reproduces the recorded body hash.

findings.summary: RoutePolicy.pool_authority was parsed but never used.
findings.fix: The admitted vaults are derived from pool_authority, so the field is load-bearing.

findings.summary: The spec quoted compute numbers the evidence did not contain.
findings.fix: The spec quotes the measured values.

findings.summary: A client guard that could never fire.
findings.fix: Replaced with real alias assertions for pools and venue vaults.

findings.summary: An unguarded mint-data index in the shared loader.
findings.fix: Length-checked before indexing.

findings.summary: The spec asked for venue vault delta reconciliation; only the output pool was re-read.
findings.fix: Both pinned venue vaults are re-read and must move by exactly the typed input and measured output.

findings.summary: Pool/vault aliasing was enforced off-chain only.
findings.fix: The handler rejects any pool colliding with an intent vault, a recipient or a venue vault.

reviews.verdict: REWORK, then all findings fixed and re-run
reviews.reviewer: independent review agent, no prior context, static review

findings.summary: Recovery was unreachable when the service was offline: the intent list came only from the service, a failed refresh erased it, and the recovery screen was disabled when the list was empty. This is exactly the outage the recovery path exists for.
findings.fix: The browser enumerates the owner's intents directly from chain through a shared decoder, the recovery route is gated on having a wallet rather than on discovery, and a failed refresh no longer erases what is on screen. A regression test fails every service endpoint and asserts recovery still works.

findings.summary: The service sorted intents by base58 string while the planner and the program require raw byte order, so roughly one valid funding set in six was rejected with a misleading 'plan rejected'.
findings.fix: Ordering moved into the shared decoder, which sorts by raw owner bytes.

findings.summary: A synchronous throw inside the approve screen's mandate effect blanked the whole interface, and there was no error boundary.
findings.fix: The effect returns early until every field is resolved, builds inside a promise chain that catches, and the app has a top-level boundary stating nothing was signed.

findings.summary: The compare screen's formatter claimed exactness but divided in floating point and could print a malformed fraction.
findings.fix: BigInt long division with trailing zeros stripped.

findings.summary: The discriminator checker's pattern skipped generic instructions, so the two settlement instructions were never covered by the completeness assertion.
findings.fix: The pattern matches generic parameters; the check now reports 13 of 13 program instructions.

findings.summary: The concurrency cap applied only to POST, so a burst of chain-reading GETs could reject legitimate work, and rate buckets were never evicted.
findings.fix: The cap applies to every request and stale buckets are pruned.

findings.summary: The commitment effect had no catch, and the expiry was recomputed on every render, so the displayed and signed expiry could differ.
findings.fix: Both fixed; the expiry is computed once.

findings.summary: A malformed base58 operator surfaced as a 500 rather than a 400.
findings.fix: Addresses are validated before use.

findings.summary: signAndSend confirmed against a freshly fetched blockhash rather than the transaction's own.
findings.fix: It confirms against the blockhash the transaction was built with.

findings.summary: The security matrix still said the service and UI did not exist.
findings.fix: Rows S17 and S18 now cite what enforces them and which tests exercise them.

not_established: No devnet deployment of the routed path and no real venue (not Meteora, not Jupiter, not an AMM).
No Pyth integration and no authenticated equity prices.
No service or UI layer, so the secret-handling and reconciled-status invariants have nothing to enforce.
No formal verification, no third-party audit, and no adversarial runtime matrix against the deployed instructions.
Two reviews were static: neither reviewer executed the validator, the suites or the checkers.
